methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents distributed capability-building outside the NoVA corridor, targeting workplace professionals with hands-on training that could enable peer-to-peer skill transfer across the Roanoke region's healthcare and manufacturing sectors.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native directly target the 'technology gap' with grassroots distribution methods, signaling potential for community-driven literacy that bypasses platform dependency in a military-adjacent region with defense tech foundations.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for distributed AI education beyond workforce training, positioning Richmond as a potential secondary hub that could bridge the NoVA-rest of Virginia capability divide through community impact focus.

signals.title: Left hand, right hand: Virginia cools on data centers even as state policy promotes the AI that requires them - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's contradictory stance—cooling on data centers locally while promoting AI statewide—reveals concentrated infrastructure investment in NoVA creating policy tension, deepening the physical and political gap between the data center capital and regions lacking AI economic participation.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Pressure on Richmond's young workforce suggests rapid but shallow AI adoption driven by platform tools and employer demands rather than deep technical capability development, risking a generation trained to use AI without understanding it.
